text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.8% today, continuing a steep two-week slide of nearly 8%. The main driver is crude oil prices—US crude dropped to $103.37 per barrel on Monday as news of Iran-US peace talks sparked hopes for de-escalation in Middle East tensions, reducing the geopolitical risk premium that had supported oil prices. For a refiner like Marathon, lower oil prices compress profit margins on fuel production, even though refineries are running at a healthy 92.8% capacity.

The decline also reflects broader caution in the energy sector heading into earnings season. On October 29th, the company announced leadership changes and a company update, but analyst commentary that same day warned investors to focus on guidance rather than headline earnings—suggesting the market is pricing in margin pressure and uncertainty about the refining outlook amid volatile crude prices and shifting geopolitical dynamics.
